title: SRE Preflight Capacity Checklist and Chaos Activation Manual
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose and scope

This document is the canonical preflight checklist and activation manual SREs must run before: major customer launches, production model rollouts, cross-region capacity changes, or planned chaos exercises that touch live inference traffic. It combines SLO & error-budget validation, automated capacity checks, telemetry smoke tests, and a safe chaos activation path. Follow this end-to-end before change windows; the procedure prevents many incidents and shortens post-incident triage when failures occur.

Audience
- SREs on rotation performing preflight sign-offs
- Oncall and release engineers coordinating launches
- Product/PMs and Eng leads responsible for rollouts

High-level run criteria (must pass all)
1) SLO health: 7-day rolling availability and p99 latency within target for the service under test.
2) Error budget remaining: >= 30% against the tenant/service SLO for the next 72 hours OR documented exception approved by SLO steward.
3) Capacity headroom: simulated 2x expected launch QPS sustained for 15 minutes without SLO degradation.
4) Observability: tracing, metrics, and logging pipelines healthy and on-call notification paths validated.
5) Rollback policy: automated rollback configured and smoke-tested in staging-to-prod path.

Preflight checklist (detailed)
A. Identification and scope\- Service(s) affected: list service names (e.g., inference-gateway, kv-cache, batching-svc, model-host-01).\- Owner and approver: service owner, release manager, SLO steward.\- Change window and expected QPS increase.

B. SLO & error-budget validation\- Verify the following (commands/examples):
  - Query recent SLO: curl -s "https://observability.internal/api/v1/slo?service=inference-gateway" | jq .status
  - Confirm p99 latency < configured threshold (default: 350ms) for user-facing generate endpoints.
  - Confirm error budget >= 30%: check ledger at /observability/slo-ledger for the tenant id.

C. Capacity probes and smoke tests\1. Warm model pools: ensure warm_pool_size >= expected concurrent models; command: ./fleetctl warm --service=model-host-01 --count=5
2. Autoscale sanity: execute a controlled ramp (see 'Ramp test procedure' below). Verify controllers respond within 60–120s and instance startup does not cause CPU OOMs.
3. KV/caching health: run 1000 prefix-lookup requests and ensure cache hit-rate >= 85%.
4. Disk and GPU memory checks: run node-healthcheck scripts (gpu-memory, nvlink, driver).

D. Observability and alerting verification\- Validate metrics ingestion and dashboard freshness: check for metric heartbeat (metric: service.heartbeat) within last 60s.\- Trace end-to-end: sample a request and confirm the span includes batching-svc, model-host, and gateway.\- Pager paths: confirm the oncall rota for the affected team is up-to-date in PagerDuty and escalation policies include product contact.

E. Safety and rollback controls\- Canary fraction configured (default 5% for large launches).\- Automatic fallback model installed and tested.\- Rollback playbook readiness: run the following (dry run): 
  1) Trigger canary rollback: ./deploy rollback --canary-id <id> --dry-run 
  2) Validate traffic steering returns to previous model variant.

Ramp test procedure (automated)\1) Prepare: configure load-generator job with target QPS = 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x expected. Each step run for 5 minutes.
2) Execute: start at 0.25x; if SLOs hold for 5 minutes, advance. If p99 or availability degrades, stop and escalate.
3) Metrics to capture: p50, p95, p99 latency, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, batch sizes.
4) Pass criteria: no SLO violations and graceful autoscale reaction at 1x; at 2x headroom observed (no more than 15% p99 uplift).

Chaos activation safe path (controlled)\- Purpose: validate fallback and degradation behaviors without causing customer-visible outages. Use for rehearsals after successful preflight checks.
Preconditions\- All preflight checks completed and green.\- Approvals received from SLO steward and Release Manager.
Activation steps (ordered)\1) Notification: send pre-exercise notification to #sre-exercises and stakeholder mailing list (template linked below).
2) Canary isolation: create isolated canary group (5% traffic) and enable chaos in canary only.
3) Fault injection: start with low-impact faults: increase kernel latency (+50ms) on model-host-02 for 2 minutes. Monitor SLOs.
4) Escalation guardrails: if p99 increases by >20% or error budget consumption rate > 10% within 10 minutes, abort immediately and perform rollback.
5) Progressive faults: if low-impact faults pass, escalate to resource pressure (reduce available GPU memory by 30%) for 3 minutes.
6) Observe and record: capture traces, heap dumps, and request/response snapshots for the evidence package.
7) Post-exercise: revert all faults and run the recovery verification checklist.

Incident review triggers from exercise
- Any SLO violation during the exercise must create a post-incident review (PIR) ticket per incident-review standards.
- Evidence package required: telemetry snapshot, trace sample, eviction logs, commands run, time-series graphs.

Decision matrix: go / no-go criteria (summary)
| Area | Go threshold | No-go trigger | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| SLO health | 7d rolling p99 <= threshold and >=30% budget | p99 > threshold or budget <30% | SLO steward |
| Autoscale | Autoscaler responds <120s at 1x | Controller errors or 503 spike > 0.5% | Infra lead |
| Observability | Dashboards and traces healthy | Missing trace spans or metrics ingestion errors | Observability team |
| Rollback | Rollback dry-run succeeds | Rollback dry-run fails | Release manager |

Operational tooling checklist (configuration snippets)
- Autoscaler config sample (yaml):
  autoscaler_min_replicas: "2"
  autoscaler_target_cpu_percent: "70"
  autoscaler_scale_up_delay_seconds: "30"
  autoscaler_scale_down_unneeded_time: "300"

- SLO alert threshold sample (prometheus-style):
  - alert: ServiceHighP99
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,service)) > 0.35
    for: "5m"
    labels: {severity: "page"}
    annotations: {summary: "p99 latency high for {{ $labels.service }}"}

- Load generator job example (k8s cronjob):
  - image: "internal/loadgen:stable"
  - args: ["--target-qps", "{{QPS}}", "--duration", "300s", "--endpoints", "/v1/generate"]

Evidence collection and postflight artifacts
- Required artifacts to attach to the rollout ticket (all):
  * Telemetry snapshot (metrics, traces) from -15m to +30m around ramp.
  * Load generator script and parameters used.
  * Rollback command log and timing.
  * Oncall notes (timeline) with actions taken and owners.

Ownership and signoff matrix
- SLO steward: validates SLO and error budget (sign-off).
- Infra owner: validates autoscaler and capacity probes (sign-off).
- Observability lead: confirms traces and dashboards (sign-off).
- Release manager: final launch approval or hold (sign-off).

When preflight fails: immediate next steps
1) Stop the rollout candidate and put service into hold.
2) Triage with owners within 30 minutes (include SLO steward, infra owner, model owner).
3) If failure is capacity-related, run triage checklist: reproduce in staging with preserved traffic profile, inspect queue/backpressure metrics, check model memory footprint.
4) If failure is observability-related, treat as a critical regression: block rollout until ingestion is restored and dry-run verified.

Playbook for common failures (quick reference)
- p99 spike with unchanged QPS: check batching behavior -> large batches forming indicates upstream slow consumers; consider temporary batch-size cap and increase warm pool.
- Autoscaler stuck scaling up: inspect controller logs (/var/log/autoscaler), restart controller if stuck, escalate to infra lead.
- Cache miss storm: enable prefix-KV cache fallback, add short-lived memcached instances, and throttle ingress.

Postflight and continuous improvement
- After every preflight that advances to production, create a short PIR if any nontrivial action occurred (even if recovered).\- Maintain a short lessons-learned note on the rollout ticket and link to sprint retrospective.
- Quarterly: SLO steward and SRE rotation run a tabletop exercise using this manual and publish results to the reliability-initiatives archive.

Templates and quick links
- Preflight signoff checklist (Google form): https://intranet.internal/preflight-form
- PagerDuty rota: https://pd.internal/rotas/sre
- Evidence upload location: https://artifacts.internal/sre-preflight/<ticket-id>
